summary: Kootenai County lookout: camp 1931, 30-foot pole L-4 tower 1933; now gone, with footings photographed. The end date is disputed (1947 or removal after a 1953 sale offer).

facts.design: 30-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Tower gone; a visitor's page captions four footings at the site

access.note: No source says whether the site is open to visitors now. One visitor reports gravel roads reaching just below the summit.

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts calls it a hike-in. One visitor came in on a road from Fourth of July Summit and climbed the southeast slope.

events.note: Idaho Fire Lookouts date; Willhite Web gives 1947 as the last year. Disputed by the firelookout.com listing.
Offered for sale to the public in 1953 and removed; no removal date given

evidence.supports: large, long mountain north of I-90, from Fourth of July Summit toward Cataldo
evidence.quote: Wall Peak is a large long mountain running the north side of Interstate 90 between the Fourth of July Summit all the way to Cataldo.

evidence.supports: 1933 30-foot pole tower with L-4 cab built
evidence.quote: a 30-foot pole tower with L-4 cab was built

evidence.supports: patrol platforms atop Swanson Mountain, a quarter mile and two miles east
evidence.quote: Patrol platforms 1/4 mile east and 2 miles east atop Swanson Mtn.
In 1944, the lookout was Charles Scott.
Known lookout personnel: 1944: Charles Scott; 1946: Art Bandon.

evidence.supports: Idaho Fire Lookouts dates destruction to 1947
Willhite Web gives 1947 as last year
offered for sale in 1953 and removed
evidence.quote: Offered for sale to the public in 1953 and removed.

evidence.supports: author came in on road from Fourth of July Summit
evidence.quote: I came in using a road from Fourth of July Summit.

notes_for_editor: Fate is disputed: Idaho Fire Lookouts and the Willhite Web page both tie the end to 1947, but the firelookout.com listing says the tower was offered for sale in 1953 and removed. The record's '1947 destroyed' is kept as the Idaho date. Access level is left unstated because no source says whether the site is open. The Willhite captions also call the summit 'Wall Mountain' in places, so searches may need that name. The record's county and coordinates are not contradicted by these sources.
